title: Native Principal Completeness Small Model
statement: Let C be a site of object size c and arrow size v and let R have coefficient size q=max(c,v,r). Equip AsSmall at size q with the induced topology and its canonical equivalence to C. Under the displayed global and slice sheafification and derived-category structures, an object N is principally locally complete for a if and only if its exact restriction is principally locally complete for the restricted section on AsSmall. Dependencies: [lem-pur-native-ringed-restriction-slices], [lem-pur-native-ringed-restriction-localization], [def-pur-ringed-principal-local-tests].

proof.text: Principal local completeness is preserved and reflected on the AsSmall model. Every compatible slice section is determined by its terminal value, hence is the restriction of a native slice section. Transfer its covering divisibility and localization test. In the reverse direction choose the AsSmall copy of each native object; the faithful derived slice equivalence reflects zero objects. No vanishing or invertibility hypothesis on the generator is used. Source: Stacks 03A0, 03CH, 03DA, 03DG and 0999.

theorem smallModelComplete
    (a : (R.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections)
    (N : DerivedCategory (NativeModules.{max c v r, c, v} R)) :
    letI := globalModulesEquivalence.{max c v r, c, max c v r, v, r}
      (K := Jsmall) F R
    principalLocallyComplete.{c, v, r, w} R a N ↔
      principalLocallyComplete.{max c v r, max c v r, r, w} S
        (restrictedSection.{max c v r, c, max c v r, v, r} (K := Jsmall) F R a)
        ((restrictModules.{max c v r, c, max c v r, v, r} (K := Jsmall) F
          R).mapDerivedCategory.obj N)
